The GPS track shows the car drove 22.6 km against a 15.9 km optimal route, +6.7 km (+42%), and took 34.2 min against a 21.4 min estimate (F1, F2) — two unexplained off-route segments, each over 0.2 km, so each segment must be individually reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

Off-route segment 21:42–21:49 drove 4.26 km where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, adding 2.69 km and straying up to 1084 m from the optimal route; no exemption applies to it, so it is an unexcused deviation under RD-1.
Off-route segment 22:02–22:09 drove 4.57 km where the optimal route covers 1.43 km, adding 3.13 km and straying up to 997 m from the optimal route; nothing exempts this segment either.

There is no in-app chat at all in this case (F8) and the rider's own message record contains no agreement to any reroute, so the driver's post-trip claim that the rider agreed (F9) is a bare assertion with nothing behind it — a verbal-agreement claim in a driver's statement is not consent.

Even taken at face value, F9 says the driver 'went round' the incident on his own initiative and reports it only in a statement written after the trip, not before the segments started, so RD-5 consent (a rider message timestamped before the gps-detour segment's start) is absent for both F3 and F4; the segments stand as unexcused and the rider's conflicting-free position is that no change was agreed.

The only traffic evidence in the file is an accident at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway 0 m from the optimal route (F12), matching the driver's stated reason (F9) — but that incident supports at most the 22:02–22:09 segment timing-wise and does nothing to explain the earlier 21:42–21:49 segment, which began 16 minutes after the report; there is no incident on the optimal route timed to the F3 segment.

The speed-band records (PIE band 5, 40–49 km/h; KLE band 4, 30–39 km/h, both 21:26–22:17 — F10, F11) are not band 1 or 2 and in any event only corroborate; under RD-4(b) they do not by themselves exempt any segment from the MVP policy.

The fare fact quantifies the overcharge in RD-2's formula: $9.45 = 6.70 excess km × $1.4101/km (F5), built from the $31.84/22.58 km distance rate in F7; there was no surge (F6) and no waiting fee (F7), so the entire contested delta is distance.

At minimum the two off-route segments' own added kilometres (2.69 km in F3 + 3.13 km in F4 = 5.82 km) at $1.4101/km come to $8.21 to be refunded under RD-2, and any segment the judge finds excused reduces that figure proportionally; the rider asks for the segment-based sum rather than the unallocated remainder.

The driver's 90-day profile carries 1 upheld dispute (F15), which meets RD-6's condition that an upheld route dispute in the window plus an adverse finding here makes this a repeated case, so the ruling should additionally send the driver's account for Ryde review.

The rider's own profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld, and a 4.6 rating (F14) — it supports nothing against her in this case and, per the policy, profile facts cannot decide the deviation question either way.

The driver may argue the ambient speed bands F10/F11 (PIE band 5, KLE band 4, 21:26–22:17) show congestion on the optimal route as well; they are not band 1/2 so RD-4(b) says they cannot exempt a segment on their own, but they colour the narrative.

The refund I can compute is bounded by the segment sums in F3/F4, not the full $9.45 in F5: RD-2 expressly does not refund the unallocated 0.88 km difference, so the larger $9.45 figure is not obtainable from these facts.

F2's 12.8-minute duration overrun partly reflects time, not distance, and RD-2 refunds only the metered distance units on unexcused segments — I have no basis to claim the time component, and a waiting-fee claim is unavailable since F7 shows $0.00 waiting.

claims.assertion: The trip contains exactly two off-route segments on gps records — 21:42–21:49 adding 2.69 km and 22:02–22:09 adding 3.13 km — so the route-deviation question must be decided segment by segment, not on the total +6.7 km (F3, F4).

The driver asserted no consent from the rider and no consent is needed for a reasonable-cause reroute, so the rider's statement that 'I never agreed to any change' does not by itself defeat segment one; the only chat record is that no in-app messages exist, and the driver's explanation is his own written statement, not a substitute for the traffic evidence (F8, F9).

On the second off-route segment (22:02–22:09, +3.13 km) the driver cannot claim exemption on this record: the one accident report at 21:26 is tied to the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway stretch already used for segment one and nothing in the traffic facts (F10–F12) ties any incident or band ≤ 2 to the optimal road replaced in the second deviation, so that segment is capped at 3.13 km × $1.4101 = $4.41 in metered fare (F4, F5, F12).

There is no waiting-fee or cancellation element to this dispute: the fare shows waiting $0.00 and no cancellation fee, so those item types are outside the award (F7).

No safety escalation is warranted: the record contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation from either side — the driver's account is a reroute explanation and the rider's complaint is a fare objection — so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 do not apply (F9).

The band-4/band-5 speed records (F10, F11) are the only congestion evidence and are not directed at the second segment; under RD-4(b) they cannot alone exempt a segment, so they only soften, not defeat, the refund on segment two.
